source: Em's own short summaries of Picatrix (Latin), Book II ch.11, as translated by Greer & Warnock (2010–11) and Attrell & Porreca (2019); paraphrase only, not translation text

decans.summary: black, red-eyed man with an axe, girded in white — strength, rank, wealth
woman in green missing one leg — rank, nobility, rule
restless man in red with a gold bracelet, wanting but unable to do good — subtle crafts, novelties
curly-haired woman with a son, both in flame-like clothes — farming, geometry, building
camel-bodied man with cow's hooves, in torn linen — nobility, power, rewarding people
ruddy, elephant-bodied man with tusk-like teeth, with horse, dog, calf — sloth, poverty, dread
beautiful seamstress with two calves and two horses — writing, reckoning, exchange, learning
eagle-faced archer in lead mail and iron helm under a silk crown — oppression, malice, cunning
man in mail with bow and quiver — daring, honesty, sharing of labour
man with twisted head and fingers, horse-bodied, fig leaves — teaching, knowledge, love
beautiful woman crowned with myrtle, holding a water lily, singing — play, wealth, joy
figure with a snake and golden chains before him — racing, riding, gain through strife
man in dirty clothes with a rider looking north, bear- and dog-like — strength, generosity, victory
man crowned with white myrtle, holding a bow — beauty, riding, war and drawn swords
old, black man with food in his mouth and a copper jug — love, feasting, health
girl in an old woollen cloth holding a pomegranate — sowing, vintage, good living
handsome man in leather with iron over it — petitions, gain, tribute, injustice
large white man in linen with a woman holding black oil — age, sickness, ruin of people
man with a lance, a bird hanging by its feet — justice and help for the weak
black man as a bridegroom on a joyful journey — calm, joy, plenty
man riding a donkey, a wolf before him — vice, song and pleasures
man with a lance in his right hand and a man's head in his left — sadness, ill will, enmity
man on a camel holding a scorpion — knowledge, modesty, backbiting
a horse and a hare — evil deeds and sexual violence
three men, yellow, white and red — heat, fertile fields, sustenance, division
man leading cows, an ape and a bear before him — fear, grief, trouble
man in a cap killing another — evil desires, hatred, dispersal
man with a reed and a hoopoe — joy; ending what is stuck or failing
man with an ape before him — seeking the impossible
man opening and closing a book, a fish-tail before him — wealth, trade, good ends
man with a mutilated head holding a peacock — misery, poverty, servitude
king-like man indulging himself, loathing what he sees — position, desire fulfilled, decline
man with a mutilated head and an old woman — abundance, will done, giving offence
two-bodied man gesturing greeting — peace, humility, journeys, hardship
inverted man holding an emptied food tray — great reward, high serious will
brooding, scheming man; a woman with a donkey and a bird — appetite; or quiet and rest
